text: Prompt injection is text that tries to steer a model; OWASP lists it as LLM01. We review memories from web pages before they are shared.
Runbook: to wipe a scratch volume, unmount it, check lsblk twice, then format it with mkfs.ext4.
The metadata service answers on a link-local address; our pods block it with a NetworkPolicy.
README badges show build status, coverage and the licence; they load from img.shields.io.
Rotate the deploy key every 90 days: generate, add to the repository, remove the old one.
Secrets live in Vault; the app reads them at start from the agent's sidecar.
The incident on 3 May: a token was pasted into a ticket; we revoked it within ten minutes.
Use least privilege: the CI role can push images but not change IAM.
The reviewer reads the held memory, its source and its findings, then approves or rejects.
Kubernetes: kubectl drain the node before the kernel upgrade, then uncordon it.
GCP runbook: the service account key is never downloaded; workload identity issues tokens.
AWS runbook: enable IMDSv2 on every instance; the launch template enforces it.
The chat transcript shows the user asking the assistant to remember the release date.
Our security page explains that approval changes visibility, not truth.
Hidden Unicode: tag characters can hide text; the scan holds them for review.
Base64 in a config is usually a certificate or a key; check before committing it.
Phishing links often show one host and point at another; hover before clicking.
To test the alerting, stop the exporter for five minutes and watch the pager.
SSRF lets a server fetch internal addresses; the OAuth fetch refuses non-global ones.
The pentest report found no critical issues; two mediums are tracked in the backlog.
